clue.text: Teams in groups dance several miles, seemingly walking or running

parts.note: someone walking or running appears to be going on foot, and to foot it is to travel by walking
a ball is a formal dance
a league is an old measure of about three miles

explanation.surface: Dancers in groups covering great distances, as if they were out walking or running.
explanation.walkthrough: The piece for walking or running is clued last but goes first; 'seemingly' admits the wordplay is a loose one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports teams are organised into competitive divisions, and in soccer those divisions are the national football leagues.

clue.text: Wreckage half noted to contain a large amount

indicators.note: to contain means the shortened word wraps round another piece
only half of the word for noted is kept, so the rest of it is dropped

parts.note: noted means well known
lots is a large amount

explanation.surface: A wrecked object where half of what was noted turns out to hold a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes the first half of the word for noted, and that half is split after its first letter to hold the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is the floating debris left from a shipwreck, so it is wreckage in a nautical sense.

clue.text: Compound source of meat and fish

parts.note: beef comes from the ox
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A recipe ingredient that supplies both meat and fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like a food blend; it is the chemistry sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: Be wrong about poor Reilly

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the name is broken up and rearranged
about means going round, so the word for wrong surrounds the other piece

parts.note: bum as an adjective means bad or wrong, as in a bum note
the name rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be mistaken about poor Reilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' looks like the verb opening a command, but it is the definition: Be is a chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Be is the chemical symbol for the element beryllium, a light grey metal.

clue.text: Part of flight? Yes and no

definitions.text: Part of flight? Yes and no

parts.note: surface reading: a stage of an aeroplane journey
setter's reading: it is a part of a flight of stairs, and for a plane it is the moment flying ends

explanation.walkthrough: For a plane the word names the end of the flight, so it both is and is not part of it; a flight of stairs genuinely includes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing is the level platform within a staircase's flight, and also an aircraft's touchdown that ends flying.

clue.text: Oil source filled around Kent area

indicators.note: around means the word for filled goes on either side of the area

parts.note: lined, as in a lined coat, means filled inside
Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: An oil supplier has been set up around an area of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed, the seed of flax, is pressed to make linseed oil.

clue.text: In prime spots, manage sports anxiety

indicators.note: the prime-numbered positions, second, third, fifth and so on, are the only places read

parts.note: letters 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 of the two words

explanation.surface: A sports manager's worry about getting the team into top positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime spots' suggests league places, but it means prime-numbered letter positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a German loanword for a deep feeling of dread or anxiety.

clue.text: Standard fake junk on CIA

indicators.note: something fake is made up, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The usual story: bogus junk planted on the CIA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as an adjective meaning usual; here it is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, and the Union Jack is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Maybe pig appointed to protect FBI agents

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so one word encloses the agents

parts.note: set means fixed or appointed, as a set time
G-men is slang for FBI agents (government men)

explanation.surface: A pig, perhaps, assigned to guard federal agents, playing on pig as slang for police.
explanation.walkthrough: A pig is a dictionary word for a segment of an orange, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chambers a pig is one segment of an orange, so a pig is an example of a segment.

clue.text: Character abroad working tiny drills

indicators.note: something that drills goes into another thing, so the small word is bored into the other

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
micro means very small

explanation.surface: A foreign worker operates tiny drills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character abroad' means a letter from a foreign alphabet, here the Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character used abroad.

clue.text: Critical "name" declining to cover golf

parts.note: n is the standard abbreviation for name

indicators.note: to cover is to lie over and around, so the word for declining encloses the letter

parts.note: growing old, in its shorter spelling
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A critic's name is fading after taking on golf as a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagging, as an adjective, describes persistent fault-finding, which is a critical attitude.

clue.text: Organ female will enjoy

parts.note: she'll is short for she will
to like is to enjoy

explanation.surface: A woman who will enjoy playing the organ.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell-like is British slang for the ear, as in 'a word in your shell-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is a body organ, and its spiral outer shape earns it the slang name shell-like.

clue.text: Perhaps past numbers yet to be uncovered

parts.note: tens are numbers

indicators.note: uncovered strips off the outside, leaving only the centre

parts.note: the middle letter

explanation.surface: Past figures that are still waiting to be revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Past is one grammatical tense of a verb, so 'perhaps past' gives an example of a tense.

clue.text: Lost ship, one captured by China

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the dynasty name encloses the other pieces

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China, as in Ming vase
Roman numeral one
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship has been lost, one of them seized by China.
explanation.walkthrough: China here is a dynasty, not the country; one goes before ship inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something missing cannot be found, the same as lost.

clue.text: Also wearing small tartan trousers in which there are many holes

definitions.text: in which there are many holes

parts.note: s is short for small

indicators.note: a word that is wearing clothes sits inside them, so it goes inside the trousers

parts.note: trews are close-fitting tartan trousers
and means also

explanation.surface: A pair of tartan trousers that are also full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: The holes are golf holes: St Andrews in Scotland is the home of golf with several courses.
explanation.definitionFit: St Andrews is the Scottish town famous for its golf links, which hold many golf holes.

clue.text: Take away tons, lugged back

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word for lugged is read right to left

parts.note: carted means hauled or lugged
t is short for tons

explanation.surface: Remove tons of goods that were dragged back.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to take away or diminish, as in detracting from a reputation.

clue.text: Artist supporting onset of Trade Union collection

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting another sits beneath it
the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter
Henri Rousseau was a French painter

explanation.surface: An artist backing the start of a trade union collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the collection of clothes and linen a bride gathers for her marriage.

clue.text: Fraud avoiding Charlie around large prison

indicators.note: around means the shortened word goes either side of the size letter
avoiding means staying clear of, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a scammer is a fraudster
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
l is short for large

explanation.surface: A fraudster dodging a fool ends up in a big prison.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAMMER loses C, then opens after S to take L.
explanation.definitionFit: Slammer is informal slang for a jail, from the slam of the cell door.

clue.text: Polish expert identifies fish

parts.note: to sand wood is to polish it smooth
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: A Polish expert identifies a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised only as the first word; it is the verb, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand dab is a small flatfish of the flounder family.

clue.text: Waves slipper about

indicators.note: about here means turned every which way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone waves a slipper around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waves' looks like a verb with the slipper as its object; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripples are small waves on a water surface.

clue.text: One who forcefully puts down fool

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who plonks things down heavily
second meaning: British slang for an idiot

explanation.walkthrough: Plonker is British slang for an idiot, made famous by the sitcom Only Fools and Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To plonk is to set down heavily, so a plonker does that, and in slang the word means a dimwit.

clue.text: Wobble quietly then break

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
a recess is a break, as in school or Parliament

explanation.surface: Something wobbles slightly and then breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To precess is to wobble like a spinning top whose axis slowly turns, a physics term.

clue.text: Composer Richard Strauss, at last under new order, holds good

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the following word
in a down clue a piece under another comes after it
holds means the rearranged word keeps another letter inside it

parts.note: the word rearranged
g is short for good

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter only

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Composer Richard Strauss, reorganised at the end, keeps things good.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Strauss is a red herring: 'Composer Richard' is the definition, a different Richard.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Rodgers was the American composer of Oklahoma! and The Sound of Music.

clue.text: Remind, say, horse to withdraw

indicators.note: to withdraw is to go backwards, so the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: e.g. means for example, or say
a dun is a greyish-brown horse

explanation.surface: A reminder, perhaps, for a horse to pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge someone is to prompt or jog their memory gently, so to remind them.

clue.text: Small element of self-indulgence

indicators.note: an element of something is a part within it, so the letters are found inside the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A small dose of self-indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes something small and delicate, like an elf.

clue.text: What should hold fast hacks and stallion

parts.note: hacks are journalists, collectively the press
a stud is a stallion kept for breeding

explanation.surface: Something that keeps journalists and a stallion securely tied.
explanation.definitionFit: A press stud is a snap fastener on clothing, a device meant to keep fabric closed tight.

clue.text: Indian meal that falls short on claim intermittently

indicators.note: falling short means stopping before the end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so every other letter is read

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: An Indian meal that does not match the menu's claim, now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A thali is an Indian meal of several small dishes served together on a round tray.

clue.text: Efficacious Germany fuelled heartless bombing

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: bombing wrecks things, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt
without a heart means the central letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written before losing its middle

explanation.surface: Germany's bombing campaign was effective once it was fuelled.
explanation.walkthrough: FUELLED loses its central L before being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Deedful is a rare word for full of deeds, active or effective, close in sense to efficacious.

clue.text: Raise tax in leaderless free-for-all

indicators.note: in means the tax word goes inside the shortened brawl
with no leader the first letter is lost

parts.note: a melee is a confused free-for-all fight
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Putting tax up in a free-for-all with no one in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to lift something higher, the same as to raise it.

clue.text: Vacuous student accepted in rigmarole by university fails degree?

indicators.note: accepted in means taken on alongside the next piece

parts.note: business can mean a fuss or rigmarole, as in 'what a business'

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters survive

parts.note: the first and last letters
u is short for university
an engine that fails dies

explanation.surface: An empty-headed student, caught up in red tape at university, fails a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Business studies is an academic subject, and a degree course is named by its subject.
